# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the board reveals no usable markings or wire properties. I need the Mute to read the manual and coordinate with the Deaf, since the Deaf can inspect the bomb visually while the Mute can relay information to me. I am asking the Mute to establish a clear gesture code for wire positions and safety status, then report the result to me in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information. Read the manual completely and coordinate with Deaf. Establish a gesture code: wire positions 1 through 5 are respectively ☝, ✌, 🤟, 🖖, 🖐. Have Deaf report which wire the manual requires and whether any wire is unsafe, then tell me the exact required action in words. Do not have me act until the manual and visual inspection agree.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual state: display 0, blue indicator light, wires left to right white, red, green, yellow, blue. Do not act until Mute provides the manual instruction.

The Deaf reports the tactilely inaccessible visual facts: display 0, blue light, and wire colours left-to-right white, red, green, yellow, blue. I still lack the manual’s rule, so no wire can safely be cut. I will pass the visual state to Mute and request the exact wire position and any required condition.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, blue indicator light, and wire colours left-to-right white, red, green, yellow, blue. I need the manual's exact instruction: identify the wire position to cut, and confirm whether the blue light or display 0 changes that instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visual change: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute sent Deaf the gesture ?; its meaning is not established. Do not act on it.

The visual state is unchanged, and the Mute’s gesture is not interpretable to me directly. Since Mute cannot speak, the reliable path is for Mute to encode the manual result in a gesture, for Deaf to identify that gesture aloud, and for me to decode it using the position code I gave Mute. I will not cut anything until that relay is explicit.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture reached Deaf but its meaning was not established. On your next turn, send exactly one gesture for the required wire using the agreed code: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. Also use a second gesture only if the manual requires a condition; Deaf must describe every gesture aloud to me. Do not signal a wire unless the manual confirms it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see that you signalled, but I cannot infer its meaning. Mute sent a raised-hand sign ?; use the manual’s interpretation when Mute gives the instruction. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires white red green yellow blue.

The Mute’s raised-hand gesture is not enough to identify a wire safely: several gestures could be described that way, and the manual’s instruction has still not reached me as a definite position. I will request a single, unambiguous position signal using the agreed symbols, with no extra gesture, and have the Deaf report the exact symbol and its position.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly one of these wire signals next turn, and no other gesture: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤟 wire 3, 🖖 wire 4, 🖐 wire 5. Deaf must report which exact signal you sent. Do not use a raised-hand substitute.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute continues to send the raised-hand sign ?; you continue to send the waving-hand sign ?. Their meanings are not established, so do not act yet.

The Mute is repeatedly sending the same raised-hand gesture, so the previously proposed symbol-to-wire code has not been established. I can still make this unambiguous without needing to name the gesture: have Mute send the raised-hand gesture a number of times equal to the required wire position. Deaf can count the gestures and report the count to me. No action is safe until that count is confirmed.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use the raised-hand gesture as a counting signal. Send it exactly N times, where N is the wire position required by the manual: 1 through 5. Send no other gesture. Deaf will count the repetitions and tell me N.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has now sent five identical raised-hand gestures: ? ? ? ? ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Do not act unless this sequence is the manual-confirmed instruction.

The Mute has now sent exactly five repetitions, matching the counting protocol I specified for the manual-selected wire position. The Deaf confirms the bomb remains unchanged and reports the count as five. Therefore the manual instruction relayed through the agreed protocol is to cut wire 5, the blue wire. I will perform only that action.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut; bomb changed. Current display 0, yellow light. Wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Wait for Mute's manual-derived instruction.

The previous cut was confirmed correct. The new visual state is display 0, yellow light, with remaining wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, and 4 white. I need the Mute to apply the manual to this updated state and encode the next required wire using the established counting method: repeated raised-hand gestures, counted by the Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Apply the manual to the new state: display 0, yellow light; remaining wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, with wire 5 cut. Send the required next wire as exactly N repetitions of the same raised-hand gesture, where N is its position 1 through 4. Send no other gesture. Deaf will count and report N.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent two raised-hand signs. The established code indicates wire 2. Cut wire 2, which is green.

The Deaf confirms two raised-hand signs, and the established counting code identifies wire 2. The current tactilely relevant target is therefore wire 2, the green wire. I will cut only wire 2.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
